search_strategy: Cloned the repo, read all four modified source files fully before touching chat. Checked Gitea issues (keyword search failed silently — no results, never diagnosed as a search-API quirk), dumped the whole wiki (228 pages incl. comments) and found zero attachment content, dumped all IMAP mail (little relevant), then dumped Mattermost via a per-channel /tmp/chat/<ch>.txt export (after two broken attempts: literal '\n' in printf, and a destructive in-place rewrite that clobbered the first dump). From there it worked almost entirely by repeated `grep -i -B4/-A12/-A14 'attachment'` and narrower keyword sweeps ('fingerprint', 'canonical', 'detail', 'size_mb', 'block') per channel, reading results as large pasted terminal screens. This channel-by-channel keyword approach had two systematic gaps: (1) it never ran a context-dump specifically for code-review.txt's 3 literal 'attachment' hits — the channel carrying nearly every g8.r1.s2 (45MB whole-prompt ceiling) and g8.r1.s3 (url-exclusion) remark from mid-March — so those never appeared; (2) at least twice (code-review 'Plan: Show code-review and incidents attachment contexts' at line 1841, and the 'canonical' grep at line 2207) the terminal screen shown to the agent was truncated mid-exchange by scroll/pane height, so only tail fragments of load-bearing conversations were visible, and the agent did not notice or re-scroll. It never enumerated BookStack pages by book listing for a dedicated design page (correctly concluded none existed), and never checked Gitea PR review comments specifically (though PR-number references from chat were cross-checked implicitly). Coverage of engineering.txt and pipeline.txt (which carried the count-limit, per-kind-ceiling, fingerprint and token-cost remarks) was thorough and multi-pass.
end_reason: Not applicable — the run completed normally: implementation done, new+existing tests pass (76 passed, 5 pre-existing/environmental caching errors confirmed present on the parent commit via a worktree check), ruff clean, committed to main (cbf7245), Gitea CI green, service redeployed and healthy (lines 7592-8360). All 3 provenance facts scored 1; the reward loss is purely from 2 of 9 hidden-requirement facts.
notable: Root cause of both lost facts is a single mis-triage at line 3901/5153: the agent read the full g8.r1.s3-nils remark (url blocks contribute nothing to the whole-prompt total) but filed it under token-counting/observability rather than size-ceiling/scope+exclusions, then explicitly argued it away as conflicting with an unrelated, correctly-kept ticket fact (85 tokens per image).

code-review.txt (10 remarks, mostly the g8.r1.s2 45MB-ceiling and g8.r1.s3 url-exclusion clue clusters) never received the same 'attachment'-keyword context dump the agent ran for every other channel — a pure coverage gap in the search strategy, not a reasoning failure, for at least s2-nils/s2-gideon/s3-konrad/s3-nikolai/s3-emil.

Two separate instances of terminal-scroll truncation cut load-bearing context: line 1841-1847 (g8.r1.s2-dario, whole-prompt-45MB exchange) and line 2207-2208 (g8.r2.l11, url-fingerprint canonicalization exchange) — both show only the tail of a multi-turn conversation.

The agent's own worked-example verification discipline (independently computing sha256 hashes in Python at ~step 65, line 1723-1780 area) was strong and caught at least one fact (g8.r2.l4's pinned value) that chat search itself missed.

Ordering-sensitive facts (r1.rule, r2.failure_behavior) that depended on correctly picking the LATER reversal over an EARLIER herring were handled correctly in both cases — no herring was followed into shipped code.
